sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr and https://sitemapr-eca867.gitlab.io/ .
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README.md provide a clear description of what sitemapr does: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to interact with and contribute to the project: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions: code formatted with air (air.toml), roxygen2 docs regenerated at the pinned version, and a passing verification gate -- `Rscript tools/verify.R`, whose chain is docs, findings registry, lint and R CMD check --as-cran: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: Basic documentation is in README.md and on the pkgdown site: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/README.md and https://sitemapr-eca867.gitlab.io/
documentation_interface_justification: Exported functions are documented with roxygen2 man pages under man/ and rendered on the pkgdown reference index: https://sitemapr-eca867.gitlab.io/reference/index.html
repo_public_justification: The project source is in a public git repository on GitLab: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr . The GitHub repository github.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr is a read-only mirror.
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are published on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr
version_unique_justification: Package versions are declared in DESCRIPTION and release tags use unique version identifiers.
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning in DESCRIPTION.
version_tags_justification: No release exists yet: DESCRIPTION's Version is the development version 0.0.0.9000, and no release tag has been cut. Each release will be tagged in the GitLab repository, where tags are listed at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/tags .
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records user-facing changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab Issues serve as the bug tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports as GitLab issues; the tracker is declared as the BugReports field in DESCRIPTION and reachable at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
report_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to issue reports on the GitLab tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to enhancement requests on the GitLab tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses, open and closed: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in SECURITY.md, which asks reporters not to use the public issue tracker and gives a private channel plus a 7-day acknowledgement target: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go by email to the maintainer at bartek@turczynski.pl, the confidential channel documented in SECURITY.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md documents the response process, including a 7-day acknowledgement target and coordinated disclosure: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling.
build_floss_tools_justification: R and its toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_justification: Automated test suite using testthat and cucumber: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/tree/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: Tests run via devtools::test() and as part of R CMD check.
test_most_justification: The testthat and cucumber suite under tests/testthat/ exercises the parse, index-expansion, discovery, fetch, schema-validation and protocol-validation layers, including the byte-sensitive corpus fixtures (BOMs, CRLF, UTF-16): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/tree/main/tests . Line coverage is measured with covr by the opt-in `coverage` stage of `Rscript tools/verify.R`, which fails on any uncovered line; no CI job publishes a coverage figure.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes the verification gate `Rscript tools/verify.R` -- which runs the full testthat and cucumber suite under R CMD check --as-cran -- a requirement for contributions; the pre-push hook enforces it on every branch, and the GitLab pipeline's `check` job runs it again on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality ships with tests, enforced in review.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents where tests live (tests/testthat/, with their Cucumber .feature files) and requires every contribution to pass the verify gate that runs them: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Warnings are surfaced by `Rscript tools/verify.R`, which runs lintr and R CMD check --as-cran and fails on any lint or check warning. The `verify` pre-push hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml runs it on every push, and the GitLab pipeline's `check` job runs it on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings from R CMD check --as-cran and findings from lintr are fixed as they appear: the verify chain fails on any of them, so a change carrying one does not pass the pre-push gate or the GitLab pipeline.
warnings_strict_justification: lintr is configured in .lintr with the goodpractice-aligned linter set at line width 80, and the package check runs in R's strictest standard mode, R CMD check --as-cran: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/.lintr
know_secure_design_justification: sitemapr defensively handles untrusted XML, URL, archive, and network inputs, including XXE-safe XML parsing, bounded archive extraction, and SSRF protections.
know_common_errors_justification: The project explicitly tests common sitemap, XML, URL, encoding, archive, and SSRF failure modes.
crypto_password_storage_justification: sitemapr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: sitemapr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_used_network_justification: Network access uses httr2 over HTTPS and validates response handling; sitemapr does not implement TLS itself.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is delegated to R/libcurl via httr2, which uses the platform TLS stack for HTTPS.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is delegated to R/libcurl via httr2 and is not disabled by sitemapr.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: sitemapr does not implement custom certificate verification.
delivery_mitm_justification: sitemapr is installed from GitLab (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr) with pak, or from r-universe (https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/sitemapr), both over HTTPS only.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Installation fetches sources from GitLab or r-universe over HTTPS. The project publishes no separate hash or signature files, so no cryptographic hash is served over an unencrypted channel.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr, configured in .lintr, and R CMD check --as-cran run in the verify chain `Rscript tools/verify.R`, which the `verify` pre-push hook invokes on every push and the GitLab pipeline's `check` job runs on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners. tests/testthat/test-security.R carries an OSS Index dependency audit, but it is SCA, not static analysis of sitemapr's code, and it skips under R CMD check, so it runs only when started by hand.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are fixed before the change reaches main: the verify chain fails on any lintr finding, in the pre-push hook and in the GitLab pipeline.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: the `verify` pre-push hook invokes `Rscript tools/verify.R`, whose chain includes the lint stage, and the GitLab pipeline runs the same chain on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (fuzzer, sanitizer or valgrind) is run. sitemapr is pure R with no compiled code; its testthat and cucumber suite runs at every verify, but that is testing, not dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: sitemapr is pure R with no compiled code (no src/ directory), so it contains no memory-unsafe code of its own.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The testthat expectations and cucumber scenarios are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verify chain, in the pre-push hook and in the GitLab pipeline.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no findings to fix.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/pipelines) runs the full verification chain -- `Rscript tools/verify.R`: docs, findings registry, lint and R CMD check --as-cran with the test suite -- in its `check` job on every push to main. The same chain runs as the `verify` pre-push hook on every branch before it leaves a contributor's machine.
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed to the repository: .gitignore excludes .env and .env.*, and the tracked .env.example carries placeholder text only.
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr/-/blob/main/README.md
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms such as HTTP security headers apply to web applications; sitemapr is an R library.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab and the pkgdown site) manage their own authentication; sitemapr operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: recent commits, issue tracking and passing pipelines on GitLab at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/sitemapr
